entries.name: S M Kaikobad
entries.biography: Interdisciplinary architect, researcher and educator; formerly a Senior Lecturer in BRAC University’s Department of Architecture and co-founder/principal of Shoho Sthapon Design Studio. His academic and practice interests include urban resilience, heritage, community, social justice, public space, informal urbanism and the relationship between built form and human behaviour. He pursued graduate study in Architecture Studies at MIT’s Aga Khan Program.
work: Graduate study in Architecture Studies, Aga Khan Program, MIT

entries.name: Tanjina Khan
entries.biography: Architect, academic and researcher associated with BRAC University’s Department of Architecture. She holds a B.Arch from BRAC University and a Master of Design Science in Sustainable Design and Building Services from the University of Sydney. Her research and practice interests include adaptive reuse, climate-responsive adaptation, urban landscapes, place-making and people–place relationships. Her professional experience includes architectural and urban-design practice.

entries.name: Upama Das Nitu
entries.affiliation: School of Architecture and Design, BRAC University
entries.biography: Architect, researcher and educator at BRAC University’s School of Architecture and Design. Her work focuses on contextual and responsive urban design, art and architecture, intangible cultural heritage, community-inclusive planning and cultural memory. She has contributed to curriculum delivery, workshops and exhibitions, and co-edited the 2025 publication project ‘New Contextualism: A Guide for Students and Beyond’.
work: Co-editor, ‘New Contextualism: A Guide for Students and Beyond’, publication project, 2025

entries.name: Golam Ahammad Sunny
entries.biography: Architect and architecture educator/Teaching Assistant associated with BRAC University. Publicly documented work includes collaborative urban-design and architectural projects, competition entries and academic teaching. His work has addressed urban fabric around transit infrastructure, water edges, community-oriented design and the relationship between architecture and cultural context.
work: Urban-design work on Shewrapara’s MRT-influenced urban fabric

entries.name: Ruaida Akter
entries.biography: Architectural graduate and teaching/research assistant associated with BRAC University. Publicly available professional information indicates experience in architectural research, teaching support and practice exposure, including an internship with Marina Tabassum Architects. She has also contributed to an academic urban-design project presented at the Institute of Architects Bangladesh.
work: Academic urban-design project presented at the Institute of Architects Bangladesh

entries.name: Mohammad Zillur Rahman
entries.affiliation: Department of Architecture, BRAC University; STUDIO PLAN.T
entries.biography: Architect, interior designer and academic in BRAC University’s Department of Architecture; also a co-founder and architect-partner at STUDIO PLAN.T. His interests include architectural design, urban design, landscape urbanism, transportation architecture, walkability and building technology. He has taught design studios and technical courses.

entries.name: Athena Rahman
entries.biography: Athena Rahman is an architect and researcher with a keen interest in heritage conservation, urban studies, and the cultural dimensions of the built environment. A BRAC University alumna, she is associated with New Contextual Lab, where her work engages with the relationship between architecture, collective memory, cultural identity, and place. Her research explores context-sensitive approaches to heritage management and the revitalisation of historic urban landscapes, particularly in Old Dhaka. Through research and design, she seeks to understand how architectural interventions can preserve cultural continuity while responding to contemporary social and urban realities.

entries.name: Monishita Mumtahina
entries.affiliation: Master of Landscape Architecture at Texas Tech University
entries.biography: Monishita Mumtahina is an architect and emerging researcher pursuing a Master of Landscape Architecture at Texas Tech University, where she also works as a Graduate Research Assistant at the XR Lab. A BRAC University alumna, her work explores the intersections of architecture, landscape, urban design, heritage, and human-environment relationships. With a strong interest in New Contextualism, she investigates how context-sensitive and human-centered design approaches can reconnect people with place, culture, and collective memory. Her interests extend to immersive technologies and their potential to inform more inclusive, resilient, and meaningful built environments.

entries.name: MD Shafi Hasnain
entries.biography: Md. Shafi Hasnain is an architect and Teaching Assistant at the Department of Architecture, BRAC University, Bangladesh. He gained recognition for his architectural creativity by winning the 22nd DOT Student Design Award 2023 in Category C (2nd and 3rd-year projects). His award-winning project, Designing a Community Center, proposed an innovative public space in Gulshan 1, Dhaka, focusing on pedestrian accessibility, elevated platforms, landscape integration, and community interaction. He also participated in the International Design Competition 2024, representing BRAC University's creative design community. His academic and professional interests reflect a strong focus on public architecture, urban spaces, and community-oriented design.

entries.name: Oindriza Reza Nodi
entries.biography: Architect whose publicly indexed professional biography identifies her as a researcher and designer, including work as a junior research and design associate at the Bengal Institute of Architecture, Landscapes and Settlements. Her public writing has addressed urban water systems and the condition of Dhaka’s canals. Her professional profile also records postgraduate study in urban/smart-city-related design at the University of Pennsylvania.
work: Published writing on urban water systems and the condition of Dhaka’s canals

entries.name: Rafa Mashiyat Zahid
entries.biography: BRAC University architecture alumna recognised for her undergraduate thesis ‘PalokPolli: Rehabilitation Center for Victims of Domestic Violence’, which received the SHAH Cement DOT Student Design Award in 2022. The project explored a healing environment for women affected by violence, using spatial privacy, landscape, water and light to support safety and recovery.
work: ‘PalokPolli: Rehabilitation Center for Victims of Domestic Violence’, undergraduate thesis. SHAH Cement DOT Student Design Award, 2022

entries.name: Sohana Khan
entries.biography: Bangladeshi architect and community-led placemaking practitioner. She completed her B.Arch at BRAC University and Master of Architecture at London South Bank University. Her experience includes work with Oxfam in Rohingya refugee camps on WASH facilities for women and children, as well as collaborations involving the BRAC Institute of Educational Development, the British Council and humanitarian/community architecture initiatives. She is associated with Article 25 in London.
work: Work with Oxfam in Rohingya refugee camps on WASH facilities for women and children

entries.name: Urbana Tabassum
entries.biography: BRAC University architecture graduate whose thesis ‘Ehyaa: The Cultural Reclamation Trail – Reviving Memory and Heritage Through Place’ (Meherpur) was selected for the Urban Design Lab Thesis Publication 2025. The project explores cultural memory, heritage-sensitive place-making, local identity and the connection between historic sites and contemporary community life.
work: ‘Ehyaa: The Cultural Reclamation Trail – Reviving Memory and Heritage Through Place’ (Meherpur), thesis. Selected for the Urban Design Lab Thesis Publication 2025

entries.name: Fatiha Tanjim Oni
entries.biography: BRAC University architecture graduate recognised internationally for her undergraduate thesis ‘Beyond Rediscovery: Alijan Jute Mill’s Future’, which received a World Architecture Community Award in 2026. The project reimagines an abandoned jute mill in Narsingdi as a productive public landscape, connecting industrial heritage, ecology, workers’ livelihoods, housing, cultural activity and the river landscape.
work: ‘Beyond Rediscovery: Alijan Jute Mill’s Future’, undergraduate thesis. World Architecture Community Award, 2026
